title: ops.polar and Polar reject documented Python float arguments
duplicate_search_queries: site:gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues Polar abs angle float Tensor MindSpore TypeError
duplicate_search_result: No exact matching GitHub or Gitee issue found for ops.polar or Polar rejecting documented Python float abs/angle arguments.
documentation_notes: MindSpore 2.9 ops.polar docs list abs as (Tensor, float), angle as (Tensor, float), return Tensor, and list CPU as a supported platform.
MindSpore 2.9 local help(ops.Polar) likewise says Inputs abs (Tensor, float) and angle (Tensor, float), with CPU support.
Same-shape Tensor controls pass for both ops.polar and ops.Polar in PyNative and Graph mode.
A pair of 0-D Tensor arguments also passes, so the failure is specifically Python float argument handling, not scalar-shaped tensor handling.
classification_notes: Not a numerical precision issue: the Python float cases fail before producing a complex tensor.
Not a CPU unsupported issue: Tensor controls pass on CPU and CPU support is documented.
The issue affects both the functional wrapper ops.polar and the direct Polar primitive, in both PyNative and Graph mode.
The active signature error says the valid call is abs=<Tensor>, angle=<Tensor>, which contradicts the documented float allowance.
